name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index (v5)
measures: A composite of independently run evaluations covering reasoning, knowledge, coding and agentic work, reported per model and reasoning-effort setting.
limitations: Version matters: v5 (27 October 2026) replaced v4.x and scores are not comparable across versions. Results depend heavily on the effort setting and on fallback behaviour when safety filters intervene. A composite hides large differences between component tasks, and third-party mirrors sometimes show slightly different decimals than the source.

name: LMArena Text Arena (overall)
measures: Human preference between anonymous model answers in blind head-to-head chats, expressed as an Elo-style rating.
limitations: Measures which answer people prefer, not whether it is correct; style, length and formatting sway votes. New models carry wide confidence intervals and are marked preliminary. Gaps of a few points are within noise, and third-party mirrors disagree on snapshots.

name: LMArena WebDev Arena
measures: Human preference between web apps generated from the same prompt by two anonymous models.
limitations: Rewards visual polish in small single-prompt apps; says little about work in large existing codebases. No current scores were captured this cycle.

name: SWE-bench Verified
measures: Share of 500 human-validated GitHub issues in Python repositories that a model resolves so that hidden tests pass.
maintainer: SWE-bench team (Princeton) with OpenAI's verified subset
limitations: Largely saturated and widely believed to be contaminated by training data; leading labs stopped headlining it for 2026 models in favour of SWE-bench Pro and newer agentic suites. Scores depend on scaffold, thinking budget and number of trials. No scores for current models were captured this cycle.

name: SWE-bench Pro
measures: Share of longer, multi-file software-engineering tasks from public and commercial repositories that an agent completes.
limitations: Several incompatible variants circulate (vendor-reported runs, Scale's standardised public set, a commercial set, V2 and V2-Hard); percentages must not be compared across them. The figures recorded here are vendor-reported as relayed by an aggregator.

name: Terminal-Bench
measures: Success rate of an agent completing multi-step professional tasks inside a command-line environment.
limitations: Version (2.0 vs 4.0), harness (Claude Code, Codex CLI, Terminus), effort level and trials per task all move the score; standard errors of 2-3 points are typical. Labs usually report their own best configuration.

name: GPQA Diamond
measures: Accuracy on 198 graduate-level multiple-choice science questions written to be hard for non-experts.
limitations: Near saturation above 90%, so differences between top models are within noise; multiple choice with four options; small question set. No results with a clearly identified evaluator were captured this cycle.

name: ARC-AGI-2
measures: Accuracy on abstract visual puzzles that require inferring a novel rule from a few examples.
limitations: Superseded as the headline ARC benchmark by ARC-AGI-3 during 2026; scores vary with cost per task and harness. No current scores were captured this cycle.

name: ARC-AGI-3
measures: Performance of an agent on interactive, game-like environments that require learning novel rules by exploration.
limitations: Two harnesses give very different numbers: ARC Prize's standard harness and a provider-adapter harness on which scores approach 100%. Results here are standard-harness figures relayed by third-party trackers, not read on arcprize.org.

name: Humanity's Last Exam (HLE)
measures: Accuracy on expert-written, closed-ended questions across many academic fields, with or without search and code tools.
maintainer: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI
limitations: With-tools and no-tools scores differ by many points and are often mixed in leaderboards; a verified 'Diamond' subset is scored separately. Some questions have disputed answers. Always check which setting a number refers to.

name: OSWorld (Verified / 2.x)
measures: Success of an agent operating a real desktop to finish multi-step computer tasks.
maintainer: XLANG Lab (University of Hong Kong) and collaborators
limitations: Versions are not comparable (OSWorld-Verified, 2.0, 2.1; strict vs partial credit; full vs offline subset). The 2.1 figures recorded here are partial-credit scores on an offline subset run by Anthropic, including for other labs' models.

name: GDPval-AA
measures: Relative quality of agent work products on real professional tasks across 44 occupations, as an Elo-style rating from pairwise grading.
limitations: Pairwise graded, so ratings shift as new models enter; version 2 and 2.1 are not interchangeable. Figures recorded here were read in Anthropic's launch posts rather than on Artificial Analysis.

name: AutomationBench
measures: Pass rate on end-to-end business workflow tasks across common SaaS tools.
limitations: Safeguard interventions count as failures when no fallback model is configured, which depresses scores for models with strict safety filters. A separately named Artificial Analysis variant reports much higher percentages and must not be mixed with these.

name: Video-MME
measures: Accuracy on multiple-choice questions about short, medium and long videos, with and without subtitles.
limitations: Multiple-choice video QA; frame-sampling policy changes results, and few rival labs accept native video input. No current scores were captured this cycle.

name: MTEB (Massive Text Embedding Benchmark)
measures: Average performance of embedding models across retrieval, classification, clustering and similarity tasks.
limitations: Self-submitted scores; the multilingual and English boards differ; averages hide retrieval-specific differences. No current scores were captured this cycle.

name: Artificial Analysis output speed
measures: Median output tokens per second measured on the provider's API after the first token.
limitations: Varies by hour, region, prompt length and reasoning setting; fast-mode or priority tiers are measured separately. Artificial Analysis is reported to be moving its headline speed measure to time per task. No scores with a clear source were captured this cycle.

name: METR 50% time horizon
measures: Length of software and research tasks, in human expert time, that a model completes with 50% reliability.
limitations: Wide confidence intervals (often several-fold); the task suite tops out below the horizons of the newest models, and METR has not published horizon figures for the late-2026 releases covered here.
